recipes.name: Delicious Feta-Crusted Salmon
ingredients_raw: 0.33333334326744 cup panko (Japanese bread crumbs) or regular dry bread crumbs

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil. Spray foil with a light coating of cooking spray, and place salmon on top.

Mix feta, mayonnaise, cream cheese, Dijon, onion powder, vinegar, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and paprika together in a bowl until smooth. Spread mixture over salmon, then sprinkle bread crumbs over top, covering completely.
Bake in the preheated oven until fish flakes easily with a fork, 35 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Delicious Feta-Crusted Salmon
raw_recipe.description: A crunchy topping made with bread crumbs and feta coats salmon fillets in this easy recipe that's sure to please everyone at the dinner table.

review.reviewBody: Mmmm- I absolutely loved this!! The feta was so good! I used sundried tomato and herb feta. I totally omitted the extra salt and it was perfect. I didn't want to open my block of cream cheese for just one tablespoon, so I used 2% fat Greek yogurt instead of the cream cheese. Unfortunately I am out of panko crumbs so I had to use regular. I only had to bake about 25 minutes- I think the time listed is too long. Watch it carefully, as you really don't want to overcook salmon. We had broccoli, steamed rice, and sliced avocado with this. Loved it!

What a great concept! This was very well received by everyone. I scaled back onion powder to 1/2 tsp, black pepper and salt to 1/4 tsp, and omitted the mustard, balsamic vinegar, and garlic powder. Baked for 15 minutes at 400, then broiled briefly to brown breadcrumbs. Perfect!

The taste was pretty good, the cook time was too long, and the color wasn't the best looking. 10-12 min at 400 then pop it under the broiler for a minute to brown was perfect for us. It was an interesting combination of flavors, may make again because we have the ingredients on hand.

YUMMM!! Even my salmon hating husband LOVED this & wants to eat it once a week!! I didn't add the salt, had to sub the cream cheese with sour cream, cooked for about 18 mins., then topped with capers (which my husband says takes it over the top!) This was so amazingly good!! Thank you for such a great recipe!!
excellent! i added diced fresh basil and tomatos, green onions, and shallots. this is a keeper! thanks for a keeper...next time this will be grilled if it's not flooding!

Wow - feta and salmon is outstanding! I used greek yogurt, no mayo, and broiled the salmon a touch at the end just to brown it. It was a great lunch the next day, too! (Hint: Only microwave cooked salmon on defrost, just to bring to room temp.)

Tried this recipe with salmon then tried it with boneless, skinless chicken breast - works equally well with both. On additional attempts at the dish, added chopped walnuts to the panko crumbs, and on another occasion added a dried Italian herb blend. Were welcome additions to the otherwise bland panko crumbs.

Quick to make, 35 minutes in the oven at 400° and ready to serve. We added a slice of Lemon to the top of each fillet for color and flavor. Substituted goat cheese for feta (either would be fine). The cream cheese held the spread together. Just the right proportions to cover each of the fillets. delightful dinner for guests with a side of buttered rotini and salad of romaine lettuce and sliced tomato. May leave time to bake a pumpkin pie with graham cracker crust.

We loved this and we're not big salmon fans. I mixed up the feta topping earlier and let the flavors marry for a couple of hours before topping the salmon and baking. I used light cream cheese, light mayo and garlic and herb feta cheese. I did not add extra salt nor garlic (since the cheese had a lot of garlic). We will definitely have again.
This was amazing. It was slightly heavy on the salt. I would cut the amount in half next time.

I had this dish in a restaurant and as soon as I got home I went to this site looking for a recipe. Both my husband and I absolutely loved it. The only ingredient adjustment I would make would be to eliminate the salt as the feta is quite salty itself. When I cook most fish I find that 20 minutes at 400F is perfect. My search is over for the best salmon recipe I have ever had.
I swapped out the feta for blue cheese. Cut the cooking time, as my filets were not that big. I LOVED it! Best salmon I’ve had in years! So good!
Once a week. At least.
Delicious but I added a little more pepper and feta cheese 😋

Delicious! This crust transformed some not top quality salmon fillets into a dish worthy of praise. The only substitution I made was table cream instead of cream cheese. Everybody in the family gave it 5 stars. This is going straight to my favorite Favorites collection.
Not a big fan of feta so i put goat cheese on it and very creamy
This was good. Not my favorite. We just didn't like the combo of feta with salmon. It was nice to try!

I typically use an Asian marinade with my salmon, so, this was a different flavor profile for us. It was delicious though! I was worried about the amount of dry seasoning because sometimes you get a texture from that much dried powder, but, this was perfect! I will be making it again.
I made this as directed, but only needed to cook mine for about 22 minutes, due to the size of my salmon filet. I liked it! It was a nice change from the one we usually make with an Asian marinade.
This was delicious and very easy - served with fresh snow peas from our garden!
